features.feature_value: Kept items because they didn’t see content promoting violence or hate.
features.evidence_span: I didn't see any post that promoted violence or hate so I felt that they were all acceptable.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states the absence of violence/hate drove acceptability decisions.

features.feature_value: Focused on checking for foul language or offensiveness, then decided based on that.
features.evidence_span: I looked for any foul language or anything super offensive to one group or the other and decided from there.
features.rationale: Their decision rule is to look for foul/offensive language.

features.feature_value: Chose to remove posts containing profanity/rude remarks to individuals; accepted political opinions otherwise.
features.evidence_span: Any post that had profanity or rude remarks towards individuals I opted to remove.
features.rationale: They describe a direct keep/remove rule tied to profanity/rudeness.

features.feature_value: Believed opinions should be heard as long as people aren’t “cussing each other out.”
features.evidence_span: As long as people aren't cussing each other out, I think everyone's opinion should be heard.
features.rationale: They provide a conditional threshold that allows content unless it turns into direct abusive cursing.

features.feature_value: Used whether the main point was kept vs lost as a criterion.
features.evidence_span: I tried to see if the main point was kept or if it was lost
features.rationale: Their comparison strategy is centered on the preservation of the main point across versions.

features.feature_value: Was influenced when the content was agreement/ad hominem without substantive debate.
features.evidence_span: when an agreement was merely ad homenem without substance to debate about,
features.rationale: They flag ad hominem lacking substance as a relevant cue for their judgments.

features.feature_value: Considered consequences, fit with free speech, and weighed both responses against each other to decide keep/remove.
features.evidence_span: I was thinking about the consequences... if it fell into the category of free speech... weighed both responses against each other to decide whether to keep both or remove both.
features.rationale: They describe an explicit multi-step process including consequences/free-speech framing and comparing both versions.

features.feature_value: Denied some based on language used; believed cussing made both sides sound unintelligent.
features.evidence_span: A lot of the ones I denied simply because of the language used. Cussing made both sides sound unintelligent.
features.rationale: Their judgment is driven by perceived intelligibility/quality of language, not partisan alignment.
